title: Further Gauss-elimination / row-rank examples
summary: Further consistency problems by row-rank reduction; an infinite-solution non-homogeneous system, a homogeneous family, and a four-variable system.
transcription_policy: Notebook order is preserved. Readable row operations and conclusions are transcribed; where the notebook is incomplete or a later arithmetic reduction is inconsistent with the original equations, a clearly labelled independent verification is added rather than silently replacing the class work.

pages.heading: Example 7 — consistency with infinitely many solutions

blocks.text: 7. Test for consistency and solve if it is consistent
The notebook eliminates the third row to zero and records the system as consistent.
The supplied page begins the back-substitution but does not finish the parameter solution.
Let \(y=k\). Then \(11y-z=3\Rightarrow z=11k-3\), and the first equation gives \(x=5-16k\).

pages.heading: Homogeneous system with infinitely many solutions

blocks.text: The notebook records infinitely many solutions.
The written annotation \(R_2\to R_2-R_1\) would produce \([0,-3,3]\); the displayed row \([0,3,-3]\) is its negative. These rows are equivalent and the final solution family is correct.
The notebook forms the augmented matrix and continues row reduction. Several intermediate entries are overwritten.
The final handwritten augmented rows display values 15 and 36 in the last column. Those values do not satisfy the original system if interpreted as final unknowns.
Independent row reduction gives full rank, \(\rho(A)=\rho(A|B)=4\), so the system has a unique solution.
